title: Percentage of Challenging Questions in 2025 PSLE Main Subject Papers
what_it_is: Percentage of Challenging Questions in 2025 PSLE Main Subject Papers

sections.label: Challenging questions in PSLE
sections.summary: Challenging questions are about 15% of marks, based on the primary syllabus, and use scaffolding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Challenging questions make up approximately 15% of total marks in each subject.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: All questions, including challenging ones, are based entirely on the primary school syllabus and do not require knowledge beyond the curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: However, challenging questions do require students to apply the concepts in novel or authentic contexts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In addition, challenging questions are often structured with scaffolding to help students attempt them progressively.

sections.label: Challenging questions and sorting
sections.summary: Missing all challenging questions caps a student's grade at AL3, affecting admission to competitive secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could it, inadvertently, become a sorting mechanism to identify students with the most resources to get the best tuition?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It should be noted that missing all the challenging questions in the PSLE paper would cap the student's grade at Achievement Level 3 (AL3) for that exam, which will impact their ability to gain admission to many competitive secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The higher order questions, the challenging questions, are included partly because there are students who can deal with them and who then need their cognitive abilities, their academic abilities assessed correctly.

sections.label: Applying concepts in schools
sections.summary: Students in schools are taught repeatedly to apply a concept to an unfamiliar question.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, throughout the approach within our formal education system in the schools, the students are taught repeatedly how to take a concept and apply it to a question that they have not previously encountered.

sections.label: Skills in formal curriculum
sections.summary: Developing these skills is part of the formal curriculum and syllabus all students go through.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These are skills, and a skill is not quite the same as a technique.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, indeed, the consideration of the development of these skills is a part of the formal curriculum and the syllabus that all students will go through.
